idiom_name: amqp091-go Channel.Consume delivery channel + goroutine range (NATS-style Subscribe callback)
implementation_notes: Go brokers push into a native channel and the consumer is a goroutine: Channel.Consume(queue, consumer, autoAck, ...) returns a <-chan Delivery owned by the client's reader goroutine, so "for d := range deliveries { handle(d); d.Ack(false) }" is the endpoint - the classic listener object disappears into the channel-plus-goroutine idiom, and the goroutine rests in the receive while the queue is idle. Clients that accept callbacks (nats.go's Subscribe(subject, func(*nats.Msg))) are the closer analogue of a MessageListener when the API offers it. Write a hand-rolled receive loop only for transports with no client library; the idiom still assumes the library owns the socket.
pitfalls: A delivery channel that is never drained stops the client's reader goroutine from processing further protocol frames (heartbeats included), so the connection can die while messages sit unacknowledged.
With autoAck=false acknowledgement is explicit: a forgotten Ack/Nack leaves the message unacked until the channel closes, and then every unacked message is redelivered.
Handling each delivery in its own goroutine (go handle(d)) abandons ordering and can outrun the prefetch limit; keep the range loop serial where order matters.
Closing the connection to stop consumption races with in-flight handlers; cancel the consumer and drain before closing the connection.
